¶ Here beginneth the Prolog of the tales of Caunterbury

han that Aprill with his showres swote
The drought of Marche hath

And bathed euer in wyn in suche licoure
Of which vertu engendereth is the floure
Whan zepherus eke with his swote brethe
Enspired hath in eueri holt and hethe
The tendre croppes and the yong sonne
Hath in the Ramme his half cours y ronne
And smale foules maken melodye
That slepen all night with open ye
So priken hem nature in here corage
Than longen folk to go on pilgrimage
And palmers to chesen strange strondes
And halowes couth in many londes
And specialli from eueri shires ende
Of Ingelond to Caunterbury thei wende
To seche the blisfull marter that is meke
That hem hath holpen whan þei were seke
It befell þat in þat ceso

on a day
In South werk atte Tabard as I lay
Redi to wende on my pilgrimage
To Caunterbury with deuoute corage
And night was comyn̄ in that herbary
Well xxix in a company
Of sondri folk be auenture I fall
In felashipp as pilgrymes were thei all
That touard Caunterbury wold ride
The chambres and hall were wide
And well were þei esed atte best
And shorteli whan the son was gon to rest
So had I spoken with hem euerich oon̄
That I was of here felaship a noon̄
And made foreward erli for to rise
To make oure wei ther as I yow devise

Or that I forther in this tale pase

That fro the tyme he first began
To ride oute he loued chiualry
Treuth honoure fredom and cortasy
Ful worthi he was in his lordez werre
And there to had he ridden̄ no man ferre
As well in cristendome as in hethinesse
And euer honoured for his worthinesse
At Alisaundre he was whan it was won̄
Ful oft he hadde the borde begon̄
A boue all nacions in prude
In letawe hadde raised and in ruse
No cristen man so oft in his degre
In Garnard atte sege eke had he be
Of Algazir and riden̄ in belmary
At lyeus was he and at Sataly
Whan þei were wonnen and on þe grete see
At mani a noble aryue hadde he be
At mortall bataile hadde he be xvⁿᵉ

In listes iij and ay slayn his foo
This same knight hadde be also

Ayenst anoþer hethen in Turky
And euer more hadde a soueraigne price
And thought that he was worthi for he was wise
And of his porte meke as a maide
He never yit no vilany seid
In all his life to no maner wight

here was al so a nonne a prioresse
That of hir smyling was simple koy
Her grettest othe was but be seint loy
And she was cleped madame Eglentine
Ful well she sange seruice devine
Entoned in hir voice ful semely
And frenshe she spake ful faire and fetesly
Aftre þe scole at stratford atte bowe
For the frensh of parys was to hir vnknowe
At hir mete wel taught was she with all
She lete no morsell from hir lippes fall
Nor wete hir fingers in hir sause depe
¶The
Wel coude she cari a morsell of mete
That no droppe fell vpon hir breste
In curtasi was set ful moche hir liste
Hir ouer lippe she so clene wept

Of grece whan she hadde dronken̄ hir draght
Ful semely aftre hir mete she raught
And sekirly she was of grete disporte
And ful of plesaunce and amiable of porte
And payned hir to counterfete the chere
Of courte to be statly of manere
And to be holden̄ digne of reuerence
But for to speke of hir conscience
She was so cheritable and so pitouse
She wold wepe if she sagh a mouse
Caught in a trappe if it were dede or blede
Of smale houndes hadde she . that she fedde
With rosted flessh or mylke or wasted brede
But sore wept she if any of hem were dede
Or if men smote hem with a yerde smerte
And al was consciens and tendernesse of herte
Ful semeli hir wymple pinched was
Hir nose tretes hir eien̄ grai as glas
Hir moth full smale therto soft and rede
But sekirli she had a faire forhede
It was almoost a span brode I trowe
For hardeli she was not vnder growe
Ful fetis was his cloke as I was war
Of smale curall abought hir arme she bare

The rule of seint Maure and of seint Benet

He gaf not of the texte a pulled henne
That seith that hunters beth no holi men̄
Nor that a Monke whan he is rechelese
Is likened to a fissh whan he is waterlese

But þat text held he not worth and oystr
And I seid his opinion was goode
What shuld he studi and make him self wode
Vpon̄ aboke alwey in cloistr to pour

This worthi man his wit ful wel be set
Ther wist no wight that he was in dette

For soth he was a worthi man with all

Of nyce consciens toke he no kepe
Of þat he fanged and had þe hier hande
Bi water he sent hem home to eueri lande

His stremes and his daunger him bisides
There was none suche fro hull vnto curtage
